sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: Cuk converter produces an inverted output voltage. In CCM it has an RHPZ similar to boost. Prefer cascaded current-inner voltage-outer control. The inner loop can regulate either L1 (input) or L2 (output) current. Output current sensing for the inner loop gives faster transient response.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: V_out = -D*V_in/(1-D). RHPZ: f_RHPZ = (1-D)^2*R/(2*pi*L2) when sensing L2 current. CCM/DCM boundary depends on both inductors. Coupling capacitor C1 voltage = V_in + V_out (in magnitude). Voltage-loop crossover: f_c < f_RHPZ/4.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: The coupling capacitor C1 carries high RMS ripple current and must be rated for the full input+output voltage. The inverted output means the feedback reference must be negative (or the sense circuit must invert). The RHPZ limits bandwidth in CCM, especially at high duty cycle.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the Cuk cannot meet transient specs in CCM due to RHPZ, consider: (1) DCM operation (eliminates RHPZ but increases ripple), (2) coupled-inductor design to reduce component count, or (3) flyback if isolation is needed.
